name: Wide, then the working shot
line: Open on the whole screen, then move in to the one panel that matters.

prompt.what: Each scene opens on the whole screen for one reading beat so the viewer knows where they are, then the camera eases in until the panel in use fills 55 to 70% of the frame width and stays there through the action. Wides take about 15% of the film and the working shot about half.
prompt.when: Fits demos and tutorials where people must see where a feature lives before they watch it work.
prompt.avoid: Two wides back to back, zooms past twice the size, and any camera move while a line is being read.

name: Close-up proof
line: The camera closes in on the one number or button that proves the point.

prompt.what: At the proof moment the camera pushes in to between 1.8 and 2.2 times over about 0.7 s, half that at hype, while the rest of the screen dims by about 40%, and the number or button is at least 4% of frame height when it lands. One close-up per promise, then back to the working shot on the next cause.
prompt.when: Fits a promise that rests on one figure, one result or one click the viewer has to believe.
prompt.avoid: Pushing in, out and in again within 1.5 s, and never land a close-up on something too small to read.

confident.ease: fast in with a soft landing

name: Wide, medium, close
line: Three shot sizes in a row, each one step closer, so the story narrows to the detail.

prompt.what: Each step of the story moves one size closer: the full browser as the wide, one panel at about 1.5 times as the medium, then one field under a loupe at about 2.5 times as the proof, each change taking about 0.8 s. Change size only when the meaning changes, and keep the eye on the same spot across each change.
prompt.when: Fits a feature best understood from where it lives down to the one value it changes.
prompt.avoid: Changing size on a timer, and moving the subject more than a quarter of the frame between one size and the next.

name: Cut on the release
line: A straight cut to a new shot size exactly as the button is let go.

prompt.what: Change shot size with a plain cut at the instant the pressed button is released, so the action carries the eye across the cut; the new shot is at least one size closer or wider, never the same size, and nothing moves for the first few frames after it.
prompt.when: Fits documentary-style demos and tutorials that want clean, honest editing with a tap sound on each cut.
prompt.avoid: Cuts between two shots of the same size, which look like a jump, and cutting while the pointer is still travelling.

name: Vertical full-bleed follow
line: The tall frame is the screen itself, tracking the action inside a wide recording.

prompt.what: Full bleed, edge to edge: the 9:16 frame rides the action at the sharpest the recording allows, pulls back while the pointer rests, and lands each follow in about 0.8 s with a spring that settles once. The action stays in the middle band every app leaves free of buttons and captions.
prompt.when: Fits Reels, TikTok and Shorts cut from an approved landscape demo, where the product should fill the phone.
prompt.avoid: Shots where the whole screen must be seen at once, and cutting it before the landscape master is approved.

confident.ease: firm spring with one small bounce

name: Vertical product card
line: A tall cut that keeps the product as a card on your brand's stage.

prompt.what: The screen stays a card with a soft shadow on the brand's stage, reaching from just under the apps' top bars down to the caption slot, and the camera follows the action inside it with eased moves of about 0.8 s. The card never runs edge to edge.
prompt.when: Fits vertical demos that should still look like a product, not a screen recording.
prompt.avoid: Products that must fill the phone; the full-bleed follow does that job.

name: Calm vertical explainer
line: An unhurried tall cut with slow follows and long holds.

prompt.what: The card stays on the stage while the camera follows in slow eased moves of about 1.2 s, closing in no further than about 1.6 times, and every result holds about 1.6 s before anything else moves.
prompt.when: Fits vertical explainers for careful buyers, where reading matters more than speed.
prompt.avoid: Hype clips, and springy follows that break the calm.

name: Square feed follow
line: A square cut for LinkedIn, Instagram and Facebook feeds, the camera tracking the action.

prompt.what: A 1:1 card with the camera following each action, closing in until the working part fills about 60% of the width and easing back out between steps over about 0.7 s. Words sit above or below the card, never across it.
prompt.when: Fits feed posts watched with the sound off for a few seconds at a time.
prompt.avoid: Shrinking a whole landscape screen into the square; follow the action instead.

confident.ease: fast in with a soft landing

name: Portrait feed follow
line: A 4:5 cut that takes up more of the feed than a square.

prompt.what: A 4:5 card that follows the action with one move per step, about 0.7 s each and half that at hype, holding after every landing so the change can be read. The extra height carries a headline above the card for the whole film.
prompt.when: Fits Instagram and Facebook feed posts that want more room than a square gives.
prompt.avoid: Crowding the headline against the card; leave at least 5% of the frame between them.

confident.ease: fast in with a soft landing

name: Tall cut-out of the action
line: A narrow card cut from the busy part of a wide recording, jumping with the action.

prompt.what: Not the whole phone screen: a tall card with a margin of stage around it, cut around wherever the action is, so it reads as a cut-out of the product. The card jumps with the pointer in snaps of about 0.25 s that settle within five frames, with a new action every 0.6 to 0.9 s.
prompt.when: Fits sound-off vertical ads and teasers that have to grab in the first second.
prompt.avoid: Text that runs off the sides of the card, and slow reading holds.

name: Full-bleed screen
line: The product fills the whole frame with no window, for honest, readable walkthroughs.

prompt.what: Show the screen edge to edge with no frame around it, and let the camera drift toward the pointer about 0.15 s behind it, covering only 30% of the distance. Text stays at least 2.6% of frame height so every step can be read.
prompt.when: Fits tutorials and long walkthroughs where reading matters more than polish.
prompt.avoid: Promos, where a full-bleed screen looks like a raw recording.

name: Split frame, then the winner
line: Two halves show the old way and the new way, then the camera closes in on the winner.

prompt.what: Open with the frame split down the middle, the old way on one side and the new way on the other, the halves sliding to meet in about 0.6 s, half that at hype; then the winning side takes the whole frame and the camera pushes in on its proof. Each half carries one idea, never two.
prompt.when: Fits before-and-after hooks, comparisons and problem-then-answer openings.
prompt.avoid: Identical motion on both halves, which hides the contrast, and more than two panes at small sizes.

confident.ease: fast in with a soft landing

name: Vertical tutorial frame
line: A tall cut that keeps the browser window and step numbers for how-to videos.

prompt.what: Keep the clean browser window with its address and a numbered badge on each step, re-laid for 9:16, and move the camera only on a click, with a steady eased push of about 0.9 s and no following. Hold 1.5 to 2 s after every step.
prompt.when: Fits vertical how-tos where viewers need to know it is a web app and which step they are on.
prompt.avoid: Short hype clips, where the window bar takes room they need.

name: Gentle medium shots
line: Unhurried shots that never go closer than one panel, for calm explainers.

prompt.what: Stay in medium shots: zooms stop at 1.6 times, take about 1.2 s and land with no overshoot, the pointer travels on slow arcs, and every result holds at least 1.5 s. Shots join with soft dissolves or a card that grows, never a hard cut.
prompt.when: Fits explainers and calm product stories for careful buyers.
prompt.avoid: Launches and social cuts, where it feels slow.

name: Two-camera interview cut
line: A filmed speaker, cut between a wide and a close camera on their key points.

prompt.what: Film the speaker on a wide camera and a close one at the same time, stay on the wide for context, and cut to the close camera only on the sentence that carries the point, staying there for that whole sentence. Every cut lands on a pause or a breath, never mid-word.
prompt.when: Fits founder stories, customer interviews and talking-head explainers shot on real footage.
prompt.avoid: Cutting on a timer, and jump cuts between two shots of the same size.

name: Slow push to the proof
line: The camera moves in slowly on the thing that matters, as if leaning closer.

prompt.what: One slow push per shot, from the working view to about 1.4 times over 1.2 to 1.6 s, eased in and out with no overshoot and started by a cause such as a click or a spoken word. The push finishes before the number or word it was heading for appears.
prompt.when: Fits calm films that want weight on a proof moment without cutting.
prompt.avoid: Pushes smaller than about 1.1 times, which read as a wobble, and never push in and back out in one shot.

name: Push on the click
line: Each click sends the camera in, and it lands as the press lands.

prompt.what: Start the push 0.3 to 0.5 s before the pointer arrives, reach about 1.6 times over 0.7 s, and land as the button dips to 95% and a soft pulse spreads from it. The pointer rests 0.2 s after the press before the next move begins.
prompt.when: Fits demos where every step is a click and the viewer should feel each one land.
prompt.avoid: More than three pushes in a scene, and never push when nothing is pressed.

name: Pull out to reveal
line: Start close on the result, then pull back to show where it lives.

prompt.what: Open tight on the finished result, a number, a card or a sent message, hold it until it reads, then pull back to the whole screen over about 1.2 s, eased in and out. The wider picture should answer the question the close-up raised.
prompt.when: Fits openings that lead with the outcome and then show the product behind it.
prompt.avoid: Moving while text is being read, and pulling back to a wide with no clear subject.

name: Snap zoom on the beat
line: Fast zooms into the product that hit with the music, for loud vertical cuts.

prompt.what: On each strong beat the camera jumps from the wide to about 2 times in 0.15 to 0.2 s, overshoots by 4 to 5% and settles within five frames, then holds until the next beat. Every snap lands on a real change on screen.
prompt.when: Fits hype edits, sale ads and launch teasers cut to a clear beat.
prompt.avoid: Calm or confident films, and snapping on a beat where nothing changes.

name: Slow pan across
line: The camera slides sideways from one thing to the next at the same distance.

prompt.what: Hold one zoom level and slide across the screen from the first subject to the second, eased in and out, over about 1.8 s, or 1.4 s in a confident film, so a row reads as one story. Come fully to rest on the second subject before anything changes there.
prompt.when: Fits a long row of cards, a timeline, or two related places on one screen.
prompt.avoid: Short or fast films; a pan quicker than about 1.4 s cannot be read.

name: Crane up to the whole page
line: Start on one detail and rise up to show the full product.

prompt.what: Begin tight on one control, then rise and lean back slightly in depth until the whole page sits in frame, over about 2 s, or 1.4 s in a confident film, eased in and out with no overshoot. It is a hero move: once per film, ideally at the turn of the story.
prompt.when: Fits the moment a film widens from one feature to the whole product.
prompt.avoid: Shots too short to give it its full length, and asking anyone to read during the rise.

name: Living hold
line: A held shot that keeps breathing with a slow drift, so it never looks frozen.

prompt.what: Through every hold the camera drifts in at a constant 2 to 3% per shot, never stopping dead, and eases straight into the next move when a cause arrives. The drift is the only motion during the hold.
prompt.when: Fits reading holds, end cards and long product moments in calm films.
prompt.avoid: Drifting across small text, or changing direction within a shot.

name: Follow the pointer
line: While zoomed in, the camera trails the pointer so travel feels natural.

prompt.what: Once zoomed in, the camera drifts toward the pointer about 0.15 s behind it and covers only 30% of the way, so the pointer leads and the frame follows. The thing being worked on never leaves the shot.
prompt.when: Fits demos with travel inside one zoomed area, such as filling in a form.
prompt.avoid: Tutorials, where a steady frame is easier to follow.

confident.ease: fast in with a soft landing

name: Zoom to each action
line: The camera eases in on each thing before it happens, then eases back out.

prompt.what: Before each action the camera eases in on its target with room around it over about 0.8 s, holds through the action and its result, then eases out, never past 2 times and never during a reading hold. Actions close together share one shot rather than zooming twice.
prompt.when: Fits most product demos; it is the studio's default demo camera.
prompt.avoid: Documentary films, and recordings where the whole screen must stay in view.

name: Tilted wide that straightens
line: The screen starts turned in depth and straightens as the camera moves in.

prompt.what: Open on a wide with the screen turned up to 10 degrees, then move in a little while it straightens to face the viewer, over about 1.4 s, or 1.1 s in a confident film, landing flat before any text is read. Use it on wides and openings only.
prompt.when: Fits establishing shots and the first frame of a launch film.
prompt.avoid: Leaving the screen turned while it has to be read.

name: Small orbit around the screen
line: The camera swings a few degrees around the floating screen for a hero shot.

prompt.what: Travel around the floating screen from one side to the other, no more than 10 degrees in all, over about 2 s, or 1.4 s in a confident film, with light crossing its surface once. Wides only, and only where nothing must be read.
prompt.when: Fits launch hero shots and the big reveal of the product.
prompt.avoid: Any screen being read, hype cuts that leave it no time, and turning further than 10 degrees.

name: Whip pan between screens
line: A fast blurred swing, the way the pointer was going, carries the viewer to the next screen.

prompt.what: The camera swings toward where the pointer was heading in about 0.2 s with motion blur, and the next screen arrives already moving the same way, settling within five frames. The direction stays the same across the join.
prompt.when: Fits fast product promos and launch sizzles, once or twice a film on a strong beat.
prompt.avoid: Reversing direction between two whips, and more than three whips in a film.

hype.ease: speeds up then snaps to rest

name: Push into a colour
line: The camera pushes into a button until its colour becomes the next scene.

prompt.what: Close in on one solid control, then keep pushing into it, speeding up over about 0.7 s until its colour floods the frame, and build the next scene on that colour. Once per film, at the turn of the story.
prompt.when: Fits the turn in a launch film, from product to brand or from problem to answer.
prompt.avoid: Pushing into anything with fine text or a busy pattern, and repeating it in the same film.

name: Beat-cut close-ups for feeds
line: Square close-ups that snap in on each click, made for busy feeds.

prompt.what: Each click is a beat: snap to about 1.8 times in 0.2 s, let a short line burst mark the press, settle within five frames, and land the next click about 0.7 s later. Show the wide only once, at the start, so the viewer knows the screen.
prompt.when: Fits square sale posts and fast feature teasers for social feeds.
prompt.avoid: Anything that needs slow reading, and bursts on a click that changes nothing.

name: Speed through the wait
line: Real waiting time plays fast, so the film never stalls.

prompt.what: Any real wait over 0.6 s, or long typing, eases into a faster speed over 0.25 s and back out again, with a small sped-up label, while the camera holds on the thing being waited for. The result itself plays at full speed.
prompt.when: Fits honest demos with loading, exports or AI answers that take real time.
prompt.avoid: Speeding up a wait that is the point of the story; show it or cut it.

name: Freeze on the result
line: The moment of success pauses while the camera moves in, then plays on.

prompt.what: At the result the picture holds still while the camera pushes in about 5% over about 1.2 s, or 0.9 s in a confident film, then eases back as the recording plays on. Once or twice per film, only on a result worth believing.
prompt.when: Fits proof moments: a report finished, a payment cleared, a task done.
prompt.avoid: Freezing more than twice in a film, and freezing on a loading state.

name: Rewind and replay
line: The recording runs back for a moment so a key step can be seen again.

prompt.what: After the key step, run the recording backwards for about 0.8 s, easing into and out of the reverse, then play it again at full speed with the camera one step closer. Use it once, on the step people would miss.
prompt.when: Fits undo stories and watch-that-again moments in short social demos.
prompt.avoid: Rewinding more than once in a film, and rewinding across a cut.

name: Snap cut on the beat
line: Hard cuts between screens that snap into place on the music.

prompt.what: Cut straight to the next screen on a strong beat, the new shot snapping in from about 105% to its own size within four frames, so each cut lands like a hit. One idea per cut, a new cut every 0.6 to 0.9 s.
prompt.when: Fits social cuts and sale ads that run on a clear beat.
prompt.avoid: Cutting off the beat, and snapping between two shots of the same screen and size.

name: Top-down descent
line: The camera drops from high above a physical product down to its detail.

prompt.what: Start high above the product looking straight down, then descend while tilting from overhead to a three-quarter view, over about 2 s, or 1.4 s in a confident film, and finish on the one detail the line is about. One continuous move, no cut.
prompt.when: Fits physical products, packaging and hardware launches.
prompt.avoid: Screen products, where there is no real object to fly over.

name: Turntable packshot
line: A physical product turns slowly on a clean stage, lit like a store photo.

prompt.what: Turn the object at one steady speed, about a quarter turn per beat, under one soft key light with a single highlight crossing it, and stop on its best angle for the name. The camera stays still; only the object turns.
prompt.when: Fits hardware, packaging and online shop product films.
prompt.avoid: Speeding up the turn partway, and busy backgrounds behind the object.

name: Handheld footage feel
line: Filmed footage with the small sway of a camera held by hand.

prompt.what: Keep a slow, natural sway of no more than 1 to 2% of the frame, at well under one cycle per second, so the shot feels present without shaking, and cut on movement inside the shot.
prompt.when: Fits footage edits, customer stories and creator-style ads.
prompt.avoid: Fast shakes, which stutter on screen, and never add sway to a screen recording.

name: Rack focus, cause to result
line: Sharpness moves from what you did to what it changed, on one screen.

prompt.what: Keep one area sharp while the rest softens and dims by 30 to 40%, then move the sharp area to the second thing over 0.4 to 0.5 s, so the eye travels from the cause to its result. Only one area is ever sharp at a time.
prompt.when: Fits a click in one place that changes something elsewhere on the same screen.
prompt.avoid: Pairing it with a torch-light pointer on the same beat; one emphasis at a time.

name: Three-layer depth
line: Background, product and foreground slide at different speeds, so the frame feels like a real space.

prompt.what: Place a soft far layer, the product and one near detail; as the camera moves, the far layer travels about 35% as far as the product and the near layer about 150%, over about 1.8 s, or 1.2 s in a confident film, eased in and out. The near layer never crosses what is being read.
prompt.when: Fits arriving at a product screen or travelling across a workspace.
prompt.avoid: Moving all layers the same amount, which looks flat, and layers with nothing in them.

name: Layered travel into the next scene
line: The camera travels through layered depth, then pushes through into the next scene.

prompt.what: Travel through the layered scene, then keep going: near layers slide out past the edges faster than far ones and the next scene rises out of the depth, the push taking about 0.8 s, half that at hype, speeding up through the middle and slowing as the new scene lands.
prompt.when: Fits scene changes in launch films that should feel like travel rather than a cut.
prompt.avoid: Flat scenes with no layers to separate, where it becomes a plain zoom.

name: Close in and isolate the panel
line: The camera goes to one panel, which stays bright while the rest of the screen falls back.

prompt.what: Ease in on the panel that carries the feature, then dim the rest of the screen by about 40% over 0.4 s, keeping the panel at its true place and size, and hold until its point is made before bringing the screen back over 0.3 s.
prompt.when: Fits busy dashboards where one panel carries the feature.
prompt.avoid: Isolating more than one panel per beat, and moving the panel while it is isolated.

confident.ease: fast in with a soft landing

name: Sharpen into view
line: A soft, blurred screen comes into focus as the story starts, then the camera leans in.

prompt.what: Begin with the product softly out of focus behind the first line, bring it to full sharpness over 0.8 to 1 s as the line clears, then let the camera push in slowly on the first thing worth reading.
prompt.when: Fits openings and teasers that hint at the product before showing it.
prompt.avoid: Leaving anything readable blurred for more than about a second, and moving the camera before the screen is sharp.

name: Lift toward the viewer
line: The chosen card rises off the screen toward the viewer.

prompt.what: With the screen staged as a flat card, the chosen item lifts off the surface by 2 to 3% in scale with a deeper shadow over about 0.35 s and settles with a 1 to 2% overshoot, while everything behind it stays still.
prompt.when: Fits picking one plan, one item or one result out of many.
prompt.avoid: Lifting several cards at once, and lifting text that is being read.

confident.ease: firm spring with one small bounce

name: Pan to a loupe on the detail
line: The camera slides to a small detail and a magnifying glass enlarges it.

prompt.what: Slide across to the small detail at one zoom level, then bring a round loupe over it, enlarging it about 2.5 times inside the loupe over 0.4 s; hold while it is read, then take it away. The rest of the screen keeps its size, so the viewer keeps their place.
prompt.when: Fits small settings, fine print and tiny status changes in tutorials.
prompt.avoid: Covering the pointer with the loupe, and more than one loupe at a time.

confident.ease: fast in with a soft landing

name: Floating screen in depth
line: The product floats at an angle in space, drifting slowly over a soft shadow.

prompt.what: Float the screen turned up to 12 degrees over a soft depth shadow, drifting about 2 degrees across the shot at a constant slow speed, and straighten it before anything is read. Wides and openers only.
prompt.when: Fits launch hero shots, openers and the closing wide.
prompt.avoid: Tilting any screen that must be read, and hype cuts too short for a slow drift to register.

name: Isometric establishing shot
line: The screen lies back in an angled 3D view to set the scene.

prompt.what: Lay the screen back in an isometric view with a solid edge for the first wide beat, hold it for one reading beat, then bring it flat before any reading begins. One angled shot per film.
prompt.when: Fits establishing beats and montage frames that show the product as an object.
prompt.avoid: Any shot that must be read, and a second angled wide straight after the first.

name: Stacked windows
line: The live screen sits in front of two more behind it, showing there is more.

prompt.what: Place the live screen in front with two stills of later steps behind it, offset up and to the right, so the depth says there is more to come; bring each back window forward over 0.5 s as its step arrives.
prompt.when: Fits several boards, projects or steps that belong together.
prompt.avoid: Busy screens, where three layers of interface turn into noise.

confident.ease: fast in with a soft landing

name: Screens step back into depth
line: One screen falls back into depth as the next one comes forward.

prompt.what: The outgoing screen recedes and dims as the incoming one moves forward from behind it, both over 0.6 to 0.7 s, so the change feels like stepping deeper into the product. The new screen lands flat and sharp.
prompt.when: Fits joins between two steps or two features in launch-style demos.
prompt.avoid: Using it for every join; mix it with one other kind of join.

name: Outline that rides the follow
line: In a tall cut, a thin outline marks the one thing that matters and moves with it.

prompt.what: As the tall frame follows the action, a thin outline traces the clicked thing over about 0.4 s and stays locked to it while the camera moves, so the eye never loses it; it lets go once the result has been read.
prompt.when: Fits vertical cuts where one control or number is the whole point.
prompt.avoid: More than one outline per beat, and outlining something the camera is about to leave.

confident.ease: fast in with a soft landing

name: Dolly zoom
line: The subject keeps its size while the space behind it stretches, for a dramatic reveal.

prompt.what: Keep the subject the same size in frame while the background stretches away or rushes in, over about 1.5 s, or 1.2 s in a confident film, so the space seems to change around it. Once per film, at the reveal.
prompt.when: Fits a dramatic turn in a launch, or a moment of surprise.
prompt.avoid: Screens with text, and using it as an everyday join.

name: Two planes sharp at once
line: A near object and a far one are both sharp, with soft space between them.

prompt.what: Keep one near element and one far element both in focus with the band between them softly blurred, so cause and result read in one frame without the eye refocusing, and hold long enough to read both.
prompt.when: Fits a product and its result seen together, such as a phone and the screen it controls.
prompt.avoid: A visible seam between the two sharp areas, and a busy middle band that pulls the eye away from both.

name: Miniature view
line: The top and bottom of the frame blur so a scene looks like a tiny model.

prompt.what: Blur bands across the top and bottom of an angled wide, keep a narrow sharp strip across the middle and lift the colour slightly, so the scene reads as a model seen from above; move the sharp strip only with the subject.
prompt.when: Fits workflow maps, office or city scenes and playful explainers.
prompt.avoid: Readable interface, which the blur would hide.

name: The pointer leads, the camera follows
line: A large pointer travels first and the camera arrives with the click.

prompt.what: The pointer sets off on a curved path, the camera starts 0.2 to 0.3 s later, covers about 70% of the distance while closing in, and lands exactly as the click lands. The next move waits until the result shows.
prompt.when: Fits tutorials and demos where the next thing always happens where the pointer goes.
prompt.avoid: The camera leading or matching the pointer exactly, or using it when nothing is clicked.

name: Guided by a presenter
line: A presenter-style pointer walks the viewer through, the camera closing in on each step.

prompt.what: Use a larger presenter pointer that moves on slow arcs and pauses about 0.3 s on each thing before using it, and let the camera ease in on each step it points at. The pointer is the viewer's guide, so it never jumps.
prompt.when: Fits onboarding, training and sales walkthroughs.
prompt.avoid: Fast pointer travel, and closing in on something the pointer has not reached.

name: Torch-light pointer
line: A soft pool of light follows the pointer, then the camera pulls back as the light opens up.

prompt.what: Dim the screen by about 50% and let a soft circle of light travel with the pointer, so the viewer sees only where the hand is; when the result appears, the light opens to the whole screen over 0.5 s as the camera pulls back to show it.
prompt.when: Fits dense screens where people get lost and one path matters.
prompt.avoid: Pairing it with a focus move or a close-up on the same beat.

confident.ease: fast in with a soft landing

name: Thumb's-eye view
line: Taps and swipes read from the screen alone on a phone-size recording, as if the viewer holds the phone.

prompt.what: Hide the pointer entirely, so each tap and swipe reads from what the screen does, about 0.2 s after the thumb would land, on a phone-size recording that fills the frame; the camera follows only up and down so the phone feels held.
prompt.when: Fits mobile app demos and app store previews.
prompt.avoid: A desktop pointer or a dot of any kind on the phone screen, and taps faster than a real thumb could manage.

confident.ease: fast in with a soft landing

name: Phone in hand, full frame
line: A screen recorded at phone size fills the vertical frame.

prompt.what: Place the phone-size recording full frame in 9:16 and let the camera follow only up and down, in slow moves of about 1 s, never cropping the sides of the app. Hold after each tap's result before the next tap.
prompt.when: Fits calm mobile walkthroughs recorded at phone size.
prompt.avoid: Desktop recordings squeezed into the tall frame, and crops that cut off the sides of the app.

name: The phone in view
line: The phone recording sits inside a plain phone shape, so the device is part of the shot.

prompt.what: Show the phone-size recording inside a plain phone frame, as tall as the frame allows above the caption slot, and keep the phone still while its screen changes in place every 1.5 to 2 s.
prompt.when: Fits app promos where the phone itself is part of the story.
prompt.avoid: Screens that must be read closely, and copying a real maker's phone shape.

confident.ease: fast in with a soft landing

name: Fly on the wall
line: No pointer at all: the camera simply watches the product work.

prompt.what: Hide the pointer and let the product appear to work on its own while the camera pans slowly from cause to result over 1.6 to 2 s. Each result holds about 1.5 s so it reads.
prompt.when: Fits automation, AI and background features where nobody clicks.
prompt.avoid: Flows that only make sense with a person's actions.

name: Follow a teammate
line: A named pointer shows a teammate at work, and the camera follows them.

prompt.what: Give the pointer a small name tag in the accent colour so the viewer sees a second person at work, keep it at a human pace with a 0.3 s pause before each action, and let the camera trail it about 0.15 s behind.
prompt.when: Fits collaboration, comments and shared workspaces.
prompt.avoid: Real people's names without permission; use a plain first name or a role.

confident.ease: fast in with a soft landing

name: Two people, one moment
line: Two recordings side by side show two people working together in time.

prompt.what: Run two recordings side by side on one clock with named pointers, lined up so one person's action and the other's reaction land on the same frame, and close in on each side's action with a gentle follow.
prompt.when: Fits real-time collaboration, chat and handovers between teammates.
prompt.avoid: A single user's flow, and two recordings whose key moments do not land on the same frame.

name: One window becomes two
line: The screen slides aside and a second view opens beside it, both still playing.

prompt.what: At the moment a second point of view matters, the screen shrinks into the left half while the next view slides out from behind it into the right half, over about 0.6 s, and both keep playing on one clock.
prompt.when: Fits a message sent and its arrival, or a change made by one person and seen by another.
prompt.avoid: Splitting when the two halves show unrelated moments, and splitting so late the viewer misses the first view.

name: Honest screen
line: The real pointer path and an almost still camera, for proof people can trust.

prompt.what: Keep the recorded pointer exactly as it moved, add no click effects, move the camera no more than a 2% push across a shot, and join shots with straight cuts. Real waits are labelled when sped up.
prompt.when: Fits proof films, honest walkthroughs and technical buyers.
prompt.avoid: Polished launches, and added click effects that undo the honest feel.

name: Card at the lens, then the product
line: A card flies straight at the viewer and the product is revealed behind it.

prompt.what: In the first 0.4 s a brand-coloured card carrying the product's name or a result flies straight at the viewer and passes the lens, and the product is revealed behind it as the camera snaps in on its first change, settling within five frames. The first readable frame lands by 0.5 s.
prompt.when: Fits scroll-stopping hooks for vertical app and product ads.
prompt.avoid: Using it after the first beat; it is an opening, not a rhythm.

name: Second view in the corner
line: A small window in the corner shows the same moment from another side.

prompt.what: Keep the main recording full size and place a second one, another user or another device, in a corner window about a quarter of the width, both on one clock so the same moment shows in both.
prompt.when: Fits a change on the web showing up on a phone, or one person's view inside another's.
prompt.avoid: Placing the small window over the action, and showing a different moment in it, which splits attention.

name: Raw vertical, real path
line: A tall, honest cut that keeps the real pointer path and skips the polish.

prompt.what: Full-bleed 9:16 with the recorded pointer path untouched; hold one scale while it still reads, otherwise follow without springs, never faster than about 0.8 s per move.
prompt.when: Fits creator-style and honest vertical cuts.
prompt.avoid: Polished promos, and springy follows that make a raw cut feel staged.

name: Over the shoulder
line: We see the screen past a person's shoulder, so it feels like real use.

prompt.what: Frame the screen past the soft edge of a person's shoulder and head in the near third of the frame, then push past them into the screen over about 1.2 s so the product takes over. The person never covers the action.
prompt.when: Fits customer stories and real-world use.
prompt.avoid: Staged-looking people and stock poses, and a shoulder that hides the screen when it matters.

name: First-person footage
line: Filmed through the user's own eyes, holding the phone or walking up to the product.

prompt.what: Film from eye height as if the viewer is the user: hands enter from the bottom of the frame, the phone or product sits in the lower two thirds, and each action is one unbroken move of about 1.2 s, half that at hype, with no cut in the middle.
prompt.when: Fits creator-style app ads and real-world product moments.
prompt.avoid: Fast shaking, and hands that cover the screen at the moment that matters.

name: Flat card on the stage
line: The screen sits on your brand's stage as a clean card with a soft shadow.

prompt.what: Present the screen as a rounded card with a thin border and a soft shadow, filling about 80% of the frame width on a plain stage, and swap to the browser window now and then across a film so it never feels the same.
prompt.when: Fits most product beats; it is the safest way to show a screen.
prompt.avoid: Shrinking the card so far that product words fall under 4% of frame height.

confident.ease: fast in with a soft landing

name: Clean browser window
line: A plain browser frame, in your stage's light or dark colours, tells the viewer it is a web app.

prompt.what: Wrap the screen in a browser frame with simple back, forward and reload marks and the real address, and no window buttons or other companies' marks; use the light frame on a light stage and the dark one for a dark product, a shade or two lighter than the stage so the window edge reads. Every camera move stays inside the window.
prompt.when: Fits tutorials and demos of web apps.
prompt.avoid: Hype social cuts, where the bar takes room, and a dark frame around a light product on a light stage.

confident.ease: fast in with a soft landing

name: On a laptop
line: The screen appears once on a plain laptop to say it is desktop software.

prompt.what: Show the screen once on a plain laptop with no logo, at about 70% of the frame width, for the establishing beat, then move into the screen for the working shots.
prompt.when: Fits office and desktop tools that benefit from a sense of place.
prompt.avoid: The device in every shot; once per film is enough.

name: On a desk monitor
line: A plain monitor on a stand, so dashboards feel at home.

prompt.what: Place the screen on a plain monitor with a simple stand for the opening wide, hold 1.5 s, then work inside the screen for the rest of the scene.
prompt.when: Fits dashboards, analytics and desktop software.
prompt.avoid: Mobile stories, and staying on the monitor once the working shots begin.

name: On a tablet
line: The product on a plain landscape tablet, for apps people use on one.

prompt.what: Show the product on a plain landscape tablet at about 75% of the frame width, with taps rather than a pointer, and change the screen in place every 1.5 to 2 s.
prompt.when: Fits tablet apps, point of sale, kiosks and field tools.
prompt.avoid: Not for desktop-only products, where it suggests a tablet app that does not exist.

confident.ease: fast in with a soft landing

name: Desktop recording on a phone
line: A tall slice of a wide recording inside a plain phone, for works-on-your-phone moments.

prompt.what: Show a tall crop of a wide recording inside a plain phone, following the action, when there is no phone-size recording; keep text inside the crop at least 4% of frame height.
prompt.when: Fits a works-on-your-phone-too beat inside a desktop demo.
prompt.avoid: Not when the product has a real mobile layout; record that instead.

name: Side by side
line: Two recordings next to each other, lined up so their key moments match.

prompt.what: Place two recordings side by side on one clock, lined up so their shared moments land on the same frame; each side gets half the width and a plain label.
prompt.when: Fits comparing two plans or two settings run through the same steps at the same time.
prompt.avoid: Recordings whose actions do not line up, and using it for two people working together or a redesign, which have their own styles.

name: Three across
line: Three versions of one flow play at once, then the winner takes the frame.

prompt.what: Run three recordings of one flow side by side on one clock, each with one clear action, and let the winner widen to the full frame at the end, over about 0.6 s, half that at hype.
prompt.when: Fits three plans, three templates or three ways to do one job.
prompt.avoid: Not in square or vertical sizes, where each recording is too small.

confident.ease: fast in with a soft landing

name: Grid of screens
line: Many screens play at once in a grid, then the camera dives into one.

prompt.what: Fill a grid with screens all playing on one clock, each a stretch of a real recording; a new tile lights up every 0.5 to 0.8 s, and the grid closes in on one tile for the final beat.
prompt.when: Fits everything-you-can-do montages.
prompt.avoid: Beats where one thing needs reading, and tiles so small the product is unrecognisable.

name: Wall of screens
line: A wall of product screens drifts in depth, then the camera moves into one.

prompt.what: Build a wall of screens turned slightly in depth, columns drifting up and down at different speeds, each tile a still from the real product; let it drift for one beat, then snap into one tile in about 0.3 s to start the story.
prompt.when: Fits openers and all-in-one-place beats.
prompt.avoid: Anything that must be read, and holding the wall so long the drift becomes the story.

name: Before and after wipe
line: A line wipes across the same screen from before to after.

prompt.what: A line with a handle wipes across the same screen from before to after over about 1 s, with plain Before and After labels, and holds on the after so the change sinks in.
prompt.when: Fits redesigns, a setting switched on, or light and dark.
prompt.avoid: Two recordings with different layouts, which show a mismatch under the wipe.

name: The email it sends
line: A neutral mail window shows the real email your product sends.

prompt.what: Show an email the product sends inside a neutral mail window with only the real subject and sender, then ease in over 0.8 s to the one line that matters and hold it there.
prompt.when: Fits notifications, receipts, reports and reminders the product sends.
prompt.avoid: Made-up subjects or senders, and zooming on the whole email when one line carries the point.

name: Terminal window
line: A plain terminal on a dark stage, for command-line tools.

prompt.what: Put the command line in a neutral terminal window on the dark stage, type at a human pace, and close in so the output is at least 4% of frame height when it lands.
prompt.when: Fits developer tools, APIs and command-line products.
prompt.avoid: Web products, and output that flashes past faster than a developer could read it.

name: Two strips, changing fast
line: Two parts of the product stacked in the tall frame, changing fast.

prompt.what: Stack two stretches of the product in the tall frame, each with its own following camera, and change them every 0.6 to 0.9 s; never three, which would be too small to read.
prompt.when: Fits many features in one vertical beat.
prompt.avoid: One feature that needs reading, and a third stacked strip, which shrinks everything below readable size.

name: Two people, stacked
line: Two people's screens stacked top and bottom in a vertical cut.

prompt.what: Stack two recordings top and bottom on one clock with named pointers, so one person's action and the other's reaction line up across the frame.
prompt.when: Fits collaboration features in vertical cuts.
prompt.avoid: A single user's flow, and two strips whose action and reaction land at different moments.

name: Patient step-by-step staging
line: A big pointer, numbered steps and long holds, so nobody gets lost.

prompt.what: Stage each step in a browser window with a numbered badge, a large pointer, a ring on every click and each key shown as a cap; the camera closes in steadily on every click with no follow and holds 1.5 to 2 s.
prompt.when: Fits tutorials, help videos and how-tos.
prompt.avoid: Short promos, and skipping a step to save time, which loses the viewer at exactly that step.

name: Clear demo staging
line: A clear, confident demo look: a tidy pointer, ring clicks and a close-in on each action.

prompt.what: A classic pointer with a slight pull toward targets, a ring on each click, a close-in on every action with a gentle follow, and real waits sped up; shots join by zooming through, matching shapes or pushing.
prompt.when: Fits most product demos.
prompt.avoid: Not when the film needs a cinematic or raw feel.

confident.ease: fast in with a soft landing

name: Snap in, blur out
line: The camera snaps into the product, then the frame rushes out in a blur to the next shot.

prompt.what: Snap in on the change in about 0.2 s and settle within five frames, then send the frame rushing at the lens in an outward streaking blur of about 0.3 s while the next shot grows out of the centre; the blur clears completely before anything is read.
prompt.when: Fits hype edits and launch sizzles where the next thing is the thing to see.
prompt.avoid: Calm films, blurring over text that is being read, and more than three blurs in a film.

name: Flooded with light
line: The frame brightens like an open lens, and the product floats up out of the light.

prompt.what: Let the frame overexpose into a soft bloom of the brand's lighter colour, one rise and one fall in about 0.8 s and never one flat white, and as it falls away the product is there, floating at a slight angle in depth.
prompt.when: Fits reveals, launches and the moment a problem turns into the answer.
prompt.avoid: Harsh pure-white flashes, more than two blooms in a film, and blooming over text being read.

confident.ease: fast in with a soft landing

name: Light across the result
line: One soft band of light passes over the card as the result appears, like light catching glass.

prompt.what: With the product staged as a clean card, let a single soft band of light, faintly tinted with the accent, cross its surface once over about 0.7 s at the moment the result appears, and never return in the same shot.
prompt.when: Fits result moments, logo cards and premium product reveals.
prompt.avoid: Repeated sweeps, which look like a loading shimmer, and sweeping a card that has not changed.

name: Iris opens on the click
line: The next scene opens from a circle on what was clicked, then the camera leans in.

prompt.what: Open the next scene from a circle centred on the button or number that was just clicked, widening like a lens opening over about 0.7 s, or 0.5 s in a confident film, with a thin accent line on its edge; then let the camera push in gently on what it revealed.
prompt.when: Fits going into whatever was just clicked or pointed at.
prompt.avoid: Centring the circle anywhere but the clicked thing, and opening circles on every change.

confident.ease: fast in with a soft landing

name: Light finds the subject
line: A dark frame, a soft pool of light finds the product, then the camera moves to the one panel that stays lit.

prompt.what: Start on a dark frame and let a soft pool of light travel in onto the product over about 0.6 s, 0.9 s in a calm film, and widen until the frame is lit; then ease the camera in on the one panel that matters and keep it bright while the rest of the screen stays dimmed by about 40%.
prompt.when: Fits curiosity hooks and premium launches that reveal one feature.
prompt.avoid: A hard-edged spotlight, and more than one per film.

calm.ease: slow in with a soft landing

confident.ease: fast in with a soft landing

name: Drift and a warm light leak
line: A slow drift on the wide, then a warm wash of light hides the change to the next shot.

prompt.what: Let the wide drift slowly in depth, then a warm wash of light tinted toward the accent drifts across the frame and the shot changes at its peak, the whole wash taking about 1.6 s, or 1.2 s in a confident film, so the change feels like film rather than a cut.
prompt.when: Fits a warm, human beat: a launch moment, a season, a customer memory.
prompt.avoid: More than one leak in a film, and any leak over text that is being read.

name: Cinematic launch lens
line: Big, polished camera work: soft-landing zooms and a slow float on wides.

prompt.what: Zooms land with a soft spring in about 0.8 s, half that at hype, wides float slowly in depth, hover gets a gentle glow and clicks a soft pulse; shots join by carrying one element, pushing into depth or whipping across.
prompt.when: Fits launches and big announcements.
prompt.avoid: Tutorials, and floating or turning any screen while it is being read.

confident.ease: firm spring with one small bounce

hype.ease: firm spring with one small bounce

name: Tight social lens
line: Tight, springy zooms that follow the action, made for sound-off feeds.

prompt.what: Tight following zooms snap in with a spring in about 0.25 s, the pointer is large, clicks get a line burst and typing is sped up early; shots join with snap cuts and whips every 0.5 to 0.8 s.
prompt.when: Fits sound-off social cuts.
prompt.avoid: Desktop demos watched at full size, and snapping in on something that has not changed.

name: Refocus between shots
line: One shot drifts out of focus as the next comes into focus.

prompt.what: The outgoing shot drifts out of focus while the next one comes into focus over 0.6 to 0.8 s, so the change feels like a lens refocusing rather than a cut.
prompt.when: Fits calm films, between closely related steps.
prompt.avoid: Unrelated scenes, because it tells the viewer they are connected.

name: Wide-angle bulge
line: A very wide lens curves the edges and makes the centre feel close.

prompt.what: Bend the frame as a very wide lens would, edges curving and the centre swelling slightly toward the viewer, and push the subject close to the lens on the beat with a 0.2 s move.
prompt.when: Fits playful creator-style ads with street-style energy.
prompt.avoid: Readable interface, which the curve distorts.

name: Lens flare streak
line: A thin horizontal streak of light crosses the frame like a film lens.

prompt.what: Pass one thin horizontal streak of cool light across the frame over 0.5 s at the moment of a reveal, peaking on the subject and fading as it leaves.
prompt.when: Fits cinematic launches and title moments.
prompt.avoid: More than one streak in a shot, and coloured rainbows of flare.

name: Dive through the click
line: Every change of screen happens by diving through what was clicked, so the film is one move.

prompt.what: Every change of screen happens through a click: the camera pushes into the pressed control and comes out in the next screen in about 0.7 s, and inside each screen it eases in on each action. The film plays as one unbroken move.
prompt.when: Fits product demos and launch films that should feel like a single take.
prompt.avoid: A hard cut anywhere in the flow; if a change has no click, plan one.

name: Carry one element across
line: One card travels from one screen into the next while everything changes around it.

prompt.what: One element, a card, an avatar or a button, travels from its place in one screen to its place in the next over 0.5 to 0.65 s, changing size and corners on the way, while the rest of the screen changes around it.
prompt.when: Fits flows where the same thing moves from a list to its detail.
prompt.avoid: Stretching the text inside the moving element, and carrying something the viewer has not noticed yet.

name: Matching shapes
line: A shape in the same place joins two screens, so the eye never moves.

prompt.what: Cut between two screens where a shape sits at the same place and size in both, so the eye stays still while the world changes around it.
prompt.when: Fits fast feature tours and before-and-after moments.
prompt.avoid: Matches where the shapes are not truly aligned; a near miss looks like a mistake.

confident.ease: fast in with a soft landing

name: The card grows into the screen
line: A card in a list grows until it is the whole detail screen.

prompt.what: On the real product, the card the pointer chose in a list or menu grows until it is the whole detail screen, over about 0.7 s, or 0.5 s in a confident film, and the detail's contents appear only in the last third of the growth.
prompt.when: Fits opening a record, a message or a project from a list.
prompt.avoid: Showing stretched content while the card grows, and growing a card the viewer did not see chosen.

name: One long scroll
line: Screens are joined by one steady scroll, as if the product were one long page.

prompt.what: Join screens with one continuous scroll, the bottom of one screen handing over to the top of the next, scrolling at a steady speed with an eased stop of about 0.8 s on each feature.
prompt.when: Fits vertical tours of long pages and feeds.
prompt.avoid: Scrolling so fast that headings cannot be read, and stopping between features without an eased landing.

name: Drag in the next screen
line: The pointer grabs the edge and pulls the next screen into view.

prompt.what: The pointer grabs the edge of the current screen and drags the next one in over about 0.6 s; the new screen trails slightly behind the pointer and settles with a 1 to 2% overshoot.
prompt.when: Fits playful demos and steps the user causes, like turning a page.
prompt.avoid: Using it on every change; save it for steps that feel like turning a page.

confident.ease: firm spring with one small bounce

name: One object carries the story
line: One accent shape travels through every scene and becomes part of each new one.

prompt.what: The camera drifts gently through each scene while one accent object, a shape or the brand's mark, hops to the next scene on a short arc of about 0.15 s and lands as part of it, a toggle's knob, a chart's bar, the closing line's full stop, so the film reads as a single move.
prompt.when: Fits launch films and explainers held together across hard cuts.
prompt.avoid: Switching which object carries the story partway through, and landing it somewhere it means nothing.

name: Soft slide to the next step
line: The next step slides in quietly, a short drift and a fade.

prompt.what: The last screen drifts about 6% the way the pointer was going while the next comes in from 6% the other side and fades up over it, in about 0.5 s, so a new step arrives without a jolt.
prompt.when: Fits tutorials and calm demos moving from one step to the next.
prompt.avoid: Changing the slide direction from step to step, and using it for big changes of place, which need a stronger join.

name: Seamless loop
line: The last frame flows back into the first, so the clip plays forever.

prompt.what: In the final beat the picture dissolves back to its first frame over about 1.2 s while the camera and pointer return to where they began, so the clip loops with no visible join.
prompt.when: Fits website heroes and social loops.
prompt.avoid: Films that end with a call to action, and a last frame whose pointer or camera sits far from the first.

name: Vertical dive through the click
line: Vertical shots joined by diving through what was clicked.

prompt.what: Join vertical shots by diving through the clicked control in about 0.7 s, each shot planned so the clicked thing and the pointer sit in the same place on both sides of the join.
prompt.when: Fits vertical demos that should feel like one take.
prompt.avoid: Joins where the clicked thing jumps position, which breaks the illusion.

name: Push from screen to screen
line: Each new screen pushes the old one out, like a row moving past a still camera.

prompt.what: Each new screen pushes the old one out of frame in one direction over about 0.5 s, half that at hype, so the film reads as a row of screens moving past a fixed camera.
prompt.when: Fits step-by-step tours with a clear forward direction.
prompt.avoid: Changing direction more than once; direction tells the viewer forward or back.

name: Opens from the click
line: The next screen opens in a circle from the exact point that was clicked.

prompt.what: At the click, the next screen of the real product opens in a circle from the pressed point, widening over 0.5 s until it fills the frame.
prompt.when: Fits demos where a click opens something new.
prompt.avoid: Starting the circle anywhere but the click, and opening circles on every change in the film.

confident.ease: fast in with a soft landing

name: Out to the grid, into the next
line: The camera pulls out to a wall of screens, then dives into the next one.

prompt.what: Pull out from the screen to a three by three wall of the product's own screens, then dive into the neighbour the pointer was heading for, the whole move taking about 0.6 s on the beat.
prompt.when: Fits feature montages that should still feel like one camera.
prompt.avoid: Calm films, and diving into a screen that has no link to the one before.

name: Clicks land on the words
line: Every click lands exactly on the word of the voice-over that names it.

prompt.what: Place every click and result on the word of the voice that names it by stretching or squeezing the pauses between actions, never the actions themselves, and let the camera ease in on each one.
prompt.when: Fits narrated demos and explainers.
prompt.avoid: Timings that would need the pauses to play more than eight times faster or four times slower than recorded.

name: Same moment, new device
line: The scene hops from laptop to phone without breaking the moment.

prompt.what: Keep the same moment on screen while the device around it changes, laptop to phone or back, over about 0.6 s, so the viewer sees the product follow them.
prompt.when: Fits products that sync across devices.
prompt.avoid: Swapping devices more than once or twice per film.

name: One take through a real place
line: A single unbroken camera move through filmed space, ending on the screen.

prompt.what: Glide without a cut through a real room, past a person, onto a desk and into the screen, one stop per beat, each glide about 1.5 s, or 1.2 s in a confident film, and each stop holding for one short line.
prompt.when: Fits brand films and launches with filmed footage.
prompt.avoid: Hiding cuts that the viewer can spot; a visible cheat breaks the spell.
